artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint by an ordained Deacon whose nomination for re-election was not advanced by the Session, holding that the Session's exercise of discretion in evaluating a candidate's eligibility for office did not constitute clear error requiring reversal. The dissent argued the proper standard of review was BCO 39-3.4 (de novo for constitutional interpretation), not 39-3.3 (great deference), because the Session applied extra-biblical and extra-constitutional attendance standards in blocking re-election.

artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.title: David Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE David Kniseley and others challenged Rocky Mountain Presbytery's approval of the public title “Minister of Church Life” for an unordained female staff member. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that “minister” has a specific technical meaning in the BCO but that the BCO is silent on generic titles for non-ordained staff, leaving that use to lower-court judgment subject to BCO 40-2(3); a dissent disagreed.

artifacts.title: Session of Crossroads Community Church v. Philadelphia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Mark Grasso and others challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's licensure and ordination of Jason Hsu, who held a stated difference concerning women deacons but affirmed willingness to follow the BCO. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery's actions; a dissent was recorded.

artifacts.title: Ordination of men who believe women may serve as deacons

matches.evidence: Believing Scripture permits women deacons, while agreeing to abide by BCO standards in practice, is not by itself sufficient grounds to deny ordination or reception in the PCA.
